note: Append a study by adding one object (newest first is not required; the page sorts by date). status: planned | promising | mixed | adopted | not-supported | insufficient | ongoing | rejected. Use only real numbers from the study file.

studies.title: Score learning plan (feature registry → labels → shadow models)
studies.question: How do we archive every input and its result so the scores can be retrained and get better as data sources are added?
studies.method: Inspection of the score change/episode logs, oid_archive tables, replay and scorecard code, C/P, walls, momentum and news archives on the mini.
studies.result: Plan only. Every score change already stores its inputs and context; missing are a fixed 15 s feature table, a label table (15 s to 30 min best/worst move, direction hit, wall touch), an experiment log and drop-one replays. Models go hand weights → logistic regression → small trees, walk-forward by day, shadow first, promoted only after beating the current score on 10+ days. Steps 1–4 need nothing paid.

studies.title: Light score on the 144 sector names (5 s replay of 10/20)
studies.question: Does the light score (trend + volume + market only) call direction on the sector names, and where?
studies.method: score_replay_wide.py re-ran 10/20 every 5 s for 144 names (light-v1.0-20261021): 15,090 holds. Graded on 1-minute bars (no sector 5 s bars). Scorecard sections: score alone, × surge, held-before-acting, × sector.
studies.result: ±3 came up 683 times and was right 43% at once. Holding ±3 for 5 minutes before acting: right 54.3% (219 holds). ±3 with a volume surge, held 5 minutes: right 67.5% (40 holds). Best sectors for ±3: Energy 52.9% (34), Materials/Mining 51.1% (45), Financials 50% (42). All nonzero scores: 38.8%.
studies.verdict: Promising for held ±3, but one day and 1-minute bars only. Keep logging.

studies.title: Core direction score: does waiting before acting help? (5 s replay of 10/20)
studies.question: If we only act when a score has held for W seconds, is it right more often?
studies.method: score_replay_changes.py re-ran 10/20 every 5 s for the core names (13,094 holds, median hold 40 s), graded on 5-second bars with no look-ahead; daily_scorecard.py held-before-acting table (W = 0/15/30/60/120/300 s).
studies.result: All nonzero scores were right 38% of the time. ±2 went from 37% at once to 43.2% after a 30 s wait (782 holds). ±2 with a volume surge held 2 minutes: 61.5% of 26 holds. ±3 did not improve (34.8% → 22.2% at 30 s, 27 holds).
studies.verdict: Waiting helps ±2 a little; the surge row is a small sample. Not enough to act on.

studies.title: Does live C/P agreeing with the score help? (same 10/20 replay)
studies.question: Is the core score right more often when the 1-minute C/P points the same way?
studies.method: Same 5 s replay and scorecard, section 'score × C/P agrees'.
studies.result: When C/P agreed: right 41.8% (4,210 holds). When C/P disagreed: 46% (845 holds). When C/P was missing (thin): 30.6%.
studies.verdict: Not supported on 10/20: agreement did not help. Having any C/P reading at all did.

studies.title: Score × momentum state (same 10/20 replay)
studies.question: Does the momentum engine's state change how often the core score is right?
studies.method: Same 5 s replay and scorecard, section 'score × momentum state'.
studies.verdict: Unexpected (decelerating did best, accelerating worst). One day; recheck before using.

studies.title: Wall magnet: is price pulled to the call or put wall?
studies.question: Above the call wall price gets pulled into it; above the put wall into that; otherwise it sits in limbo unless volume picks up. True?
studies.method: 82,190 ticker-minutes over 325 ticker-days (9/25–10/20), FlashAlpha walls harvested from 1,045 stored snapshots (latest earlier the same day, no look-ahead), 1-minute SIP bars, compared with a no-magnet chance rate.
studies.result: Just above the call wall, price touched it 46.9% within 5 min vs 44.9% by chance; just above the put wall 9.2% vs 9.9%. No extra 'limbo' away from walls. A 1-minute rvol of 3× or more roughly triples breakout odds everywhere: away from walls, 15-minute breakouts go from 8.7% to 26.7%.
studies.verdict: Mostly not supported. Volume is the real switch.

studies.title: Where the FlashAlpha calls go
studies.question: Which jobs use the 2,500-a-day FlashAlpha quota, and will the full-day wall refresh fit?
studies.method: Rebuilt from mini logs and X-RateLimit-Remaining after each call (quota day 5 PM–5 PM PT).
studies.result: About 2,122 of 2,500 calls used by 4:32 PM PT: VIX ~700 (33%), oil futures 450 (21%), walls 325 (15%, started 11:20 AM), agent routines ~650 (31%). A full wall day projects to ~2,850, over the cap. Free changes could save 1,300–1,500 calls a day.
studies.verdict: Walls were not the big user; VIX and futures were. Free savings listed; nothing bought.

studies.title: Options-wall data: where to get more
studies.question: Can we get walls for more names, or fresher, without a big new bill?
studies.method: Vendor pricing read from public sites on 10/20; UW GEX tested on NVDA and OXY.
studies.result: FlashAlpha Alpha is $1,499/mo. Free options: trim VIX/futures/agent calls, UW GEX levels (already paid, different method: NVDA call wall 230 at UW vs 220 at FA), or our own walls from Alpaca open interest (~300 calls a day for 144 names, OI 2 days old).
studies.verdict: Nothing bought. Free savings first; Alpaca OI walls are the $0 path.

studies.title: Sector options universe (which 144 names to add)
studies.question: Which liquid option names in each sector should the live page scan?
studies.method: Unusual Whales stock screener ~12:55 PM PT 10/20; 30-day average option volume, core ≥ 20k contracts/day.
studies.result: 270 rows screened, 197 core; starter list of 144 names (≤10 per sector) across 16 sectors. WDC, STX and SNDK excluded.
studies.verdict: Adopted: these are the sector names in the Table view.

studies.title: Direction score first look (15-minute grading, live 10/20)
studies.question: Does the −3…+3 score line up with forward returns at 5 minutes to the close?
studies.method: 1,610 live score rows on 10/20 (61 tickers, config v1-20261019) graded at +5 m to the close; 10/19 replayed as a backfill.
studies.result: On 10/20 the score ran opposite to forward returns: nonzero hit rate 34% at 5 m, 32% at 1 h, 27.5% at the close; correlation of raw score with the close return −0.39. One session of correlated tickers. Research Bot's DS1 check: INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
studies.verdict: An anecdote, not evidence. Led to the 5 s change log and hold-based grading.

studies.title: Does the 15 s call/put buy ratio predict price? (MU, CRWV)
studies.question: Jeffrey saw MU's 15 s C/P lead price. Does it predict the next minute?
studies.method: Alpaca historical OPRA trades sided with the tick rule, 15 s windows, MU and CRWV full session 10/19; checked against the live chip (77% side agreement).
studies.result: C/P moves with price in the same minute (correlation about 0.4–0.6) but not the next minute (MU −0.008, CRWV −0.01). Ratio > 1 then next minute up: MU 48% vs a 46% base. CRWV's big ratios were mostly thin data (15% of windows had $0 put buys).

studies.title: Real-time options aggressor at 10–15 s: how to build it
studies.question: How can we see call/put buying and selling live, every 10–15 s, without a new subscription?
studies.method: Vendor and API review; Alpaca OPRA limits; published accuracy of the quote rule.
studies.result: Use the Alpaca OPRA feed already paid for (one websocket, up to 1,000 quoted contracts). Quote rule is right about 83% on trades it can classify (~80% over all trades).
studies.verdict: Adopted: this is the live 15 s / 1 m C/P chip.

studies.title: Live page: options vs Robinhood latency
studies.question: How far behind Robinhood is the mini's live page?
studies.method: Loopback sampling on the mini 11:00–11:16 AM PT 10/19, compared with the Robinhood connector (read-only).
studies.result: The options table was not slow but frozen: the OPRA websocket had 0 subscribed contracts since 8:48:11 AM PT.
studies.verdict: Problem found: the options feed was frozen, not slow. See the file for the details.

studies.title: Ladder-scalp dry run: do surges into a thin book reach the next wall?
studies.question: Volume surge + thin order book on the move side → price runs to the next resting wall?
studies.method: Robinhood L2 snapshots at surge time (10/19–10/20, 72 real snapshots), graded on 1-minute bars: wall reached vs $0.50 stop. Stock moves only.
studies.result: Thin book: wall reached 6 of 14 (43%). Not thin: 26 of 58 (45%).
studies.verdict: No edge from 'thin' so far; small sample. Still collecting.

studies.title: Confidence log and weekly calibration (Rose / Hal)
studies.question: When the desk says 60% sure, is it right 60% of the time?
studies.method: Every decision logs a stated probability; weekly report scores it (Brier, reliability buckets). Report 2026-42.
studies.result: 178 decided, 118 scored: mean confidence 36% vs hit rate 34%, Brier 0.224. Overconfident in the 0.5–0.6 bucket (said 52%, hit 38%, n = 8). Rose: said 41%, hit 22% (n = 18, small sample).
studies.verdict: Roughly calibrated overall; a bit overconfident above 50%. Weekly, scorekeeping only.

studies.title: Jev sub-100 ms crypto model
studies.question: Could RohOnChain's Jev crypto buy/sell model help OID?
studies.method: Review of the design and independent paper tests.
studies.result: Direction calls near random: AUC 0.46–0.49. Speed is not OID's bottleneck.
studies.verdict: Rejected. Started the confidence log instead.

studies.title: Vendor bake-off: Unusual Whales vs Quant Data
studies.question: Is Quant Data worth adding for full options tape, net-premium drift and wall-break confirmation?
studies.method: Feature and API comparison against the Unusual Whales MCP the desk already pays for.
studies.result: The gaps were mostly under-used UW features, not a missing vendor.
studies.verdict: Stay UW-only; do not add Quant Data.
